title: Prove clean image and PostgreSQL bootstrap

commits.purpose: build the image from the frozen lock and pin every image digest
serialise release tasks so concurrent containers cannot race migrations
make the release-task runner importable when run as a script

image.interpreter: CPython 3.12.14 (the only platform G0-01 qualified the lock for)

acceptance.observed: exit 0; builder stage ran docker/lock-requirements.py and installed the lock with --require-hashes; the direct spaCy wheel was fetched from the URL recorded in the artifact inventory; the production stage exported manifest sha256:facdac25e17569e3d0b3deab59ba0dd83306b56eba783b8ee7d80332c03edd12

both exit 0. The rendered configuration shows the digest-pinned service images (postgres, redis, nginx), the two built services' build arguments, and the scheduler's HORILLA_SKIP_RELEASE_TASKS: "1". The production overlay declares env_file: .env, so the validation used a temporary .env holding obviously fake values; it was deleted afterwards and is not committed (it is gitignored).

acceptance.command: docker compose exec -T web python manage.py check
acceptance.observed: exit 0; "System check identified no issues (0 silenced)." The container was still in its static-collection phase at that moment, which is why the check is run through exec rather than through a health gate.

acceptance.criterion: repeated bootstrap has no migration race

parts.observed: 250 rows in django_migrations after the first bootstrap; the winner's log applies every migration and reaches "Starting server..."
a container started against the already-migrated database acquires the release lock immediately, reports "No migrations to apply." and starts serving

three containers started at once against an empty database: all three exited 0. One acquired the release lock after 0.0s and applied the migrations; the other two waited 298.9s and 317.9s for the lock and then found "No migrations to apply." Total wall clock 349s.

prior_failure_preserved.measured_before_the_fix: Two containers started together against an empty database: one exited 0, the other exited 1 with psycopg2.errors.UniqueViolation on "pg_type_typname_nsp_index" (Key (typname, typnamespace)=(django_migrations, 2200) already exists) and django.db.migrations.exceptions.MigrationSchemaMissing, i.e. both tried to create the migrations table.

acceptance.observed: Every startup begins with "Qdrat image build: version=2.1.6 revision=da6f808bb7a2646a5d851afc696bba62ea8b4b53 built=2026-09-21T20:20:00Z". Those three values are the image's QDRAT_BUILD_* environment variables, which come from the build arguments, and the same revision is on the image label org.opencontainers.image.revision. The image itself is identified by digest sha256:facdac25e17569e3d0b3deab59ba0dd83306b56eba783b8ee7d80332c03edd12. A container cannot read its own digest from inside, so the binding is: recorded log + recorded image digest + matching revision in both.

os_package_inventory.observed: 157 installed Debian packages with exact versions, from the digest-pinned python:3.12-slim base plus the runtime apt list in the Dockerfile

probes.readiness: GET /ready/ -> {"status": "ok", "database": "ok", "cache": "ok", "scheduler": "missing"}. The scheduler field is expected here: only the web service was started. /ready/ reports the scheduler as missing rather than failing, which is the documented default (HORILLA_REQUIRE_SCHEDULER is off).

specgrain.context: 7 selected sources, 11716 of 20000 tokens; the 167 KB artifact inventory was declared optional and omitted rather than evicting a required source

artifact_digests_at_the_head.canonicalisation: sha256 over UTF-8 bytes with CRLF normalised to LF, the same rule the G0-01 repair established

findings.summary: Two containers of this image started together against an empty database raced on migrations; one died.
findings.fix: docker/release_tasks.py runs migrate and collectstatic under a session-level PostgreSQL advisory lock (commit 1ad211f0).
findings.rechecked: three containers, empty database, all exit 0, two of them waiting on the lock (evidence/g0-02/race-after-serialisation-*.log)

findings.summary: The new release-task runner could not import the application when executed the way the entrypoint executes it.
findings.evidence: The first after-fix probe failed on every container with "ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'horilla'": running python docker/release_tasks.py puts docker/ on sys.path, not the project root.
findings.fix: The module binds the project root explicitly (commit da6f808b), with a test that executes it from docker/ in a fresh interpreter.
findings.note: This was caught by the proof and not by the unit tests, which is why the proof is not optional.

findings.summary: The web healthcheck declares the container unhealthy during a legitimate first bootstrap on this host.
findings.evidence: docker-compose.yml gives web interval 30s, start_period 60s, retries 3, so it reports unhealthy about 150s after start. Measured on this host with the source bind-mounted: 8m51s from container start to 'Listening at http://0.0.0.0:8000' on an empty database (bootstrap-1), and 3m47s for a repeat bootstrap that applied no migrations at all, because collectstatic still walks the bind mount (bootstrap-2-repeat). docker compose up --wait therefore reported 'container qdrat-web-1 is unhealthy' while the bootstrap was in fact progressing, and the same container became healthy at 19:58:45 and answered /health/ and /ready/ with 200.
findings.why_not_fixed_here: Choosing a longer grace period trades false-unhealthy for slower detection of a genuinely broken container. That is a deployment-policy decision, not something the evidence forces, so the measurement is recorded and the decision is named as a successor obligation (QDRAT-DEV-HEALTHCHECK-BUDGET) instead of being made silently in this grain.

findings.summary: /ready/ reports scheduler "missing" whenever only the web service runs.
findings.evidence: {"status": "ok", "database": "ok", "cache": "ok", "scheduler": "missing"} with only web, db and redis started.
findings.disposition: Expected: the scheduler is a separate service and /ready/ deliberately does not fail on it unless HORILLA_REQUIRE_SCHEDULER is set. Recorded so the value is not mistaken for a defect in the bootstrap.

findings.summary: No independent review of this change.
findings.evidence: Open Code Review v1.12.8 (sha256 150812b67201e5a5fffc4acdd05a468b0737a10606ae109f0ba08541c1bc4a18) is present and its deterministic preview runs, but the review itself needs an LLM endpoint credential (OCR_LLM_URL/OCR_LLM_TOKEN/OCR_LLM_MODEL or ~/.opencodereview/config.json) that does not exist in this environment. The environment's only model credential serves Jev decision models, which answer typed questions rather than reviewing a diff.
findings.disposition: Recorded as REVIEW_UNAVAILABLE. Chapter 41 treats that as not-approval, so G0-02 cannot be called independently verified and the accepted-head item cannot honestly be produced for it yet.

findings.evidence: The inherited workflows still trigger on dev/v2.0 and 2.0 only.
findings.disposition: Carried forward; the G0 exit requires CI on the actual Qdrat PR base and that work is not part of this grain.

not_claimed: that the development host's measured bootstrap time generalises to other hardware
